subject: Music Production
title: The Wall of Sound: Phil Spector's Method
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Wall of Sound: Phil Spector's Method usable.

hook.text: Phil Spector crammed dozens of musicians into Gold Star Studios and recorded them all at once.

buildup.text: Multiple guitars, pianos, bass, drums, and strings played in unison, creating a massive layered sound.

discovery.text: The resulting mix was a dense, reverb-drenched mono wall that overwhelmed radio speakers with power.

twist.text: Spector insisted on mono because he wanted total control over exactly what listeners heard.

climax.text: The Wall of Sound technique influenced decades of pop, rock, and electronic music production.

punchline.text: Dozens of musicians in one room made pop's biggest sound.

quiz.question: Why did Phil Spector prefer mono mixes?
options: He wanted total control over exactly what listeners heard
Stereo didn't exist during his era
